propositions: Subagents spawn unbounded CPU load generators (python -c 'while True: pass') that outlive the investigation session and become PPID-1 orphans, running uncontrolled for days at high CPU cost.
38 workers spawned in a single batch on 2026-08-22 were orphaned to PID 1 and ran continuously for four days at ~1341% combined CPU, accumulating ~138,000 CPU-seconds and degrading host usability.

Agent guidance must require background processes be bounded at spawn time (e.g. 'timeout 120 python -c ...') with process-group teardown (trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM) and explicit reaping including error paths to prevent PPID-1 orphans.

A detection check identifies PPID-1 processes with accumulated CPU time exceeding a configurable threshold (default 3600 CPU-seconds) while filtering system-owned executables to avoid noise from OS daemons.

The detection check is injectable for testing, excludes system paths by default (with --include-system override), and is exercised both via unit tests and live read-only smoke assertions against real process state.
